declarations.docstring: An auxiliary type relating two objects of the same quiver-indexed construction over a commutative semiring.
The linear equivalence supplied at a vertex by an auxiliary equivalence.
The vertexwise linear equivalences commute with the linear maps induced by every quiver morphism.
A commuting family of vertexwise linear equivalences determines a nonempty auxiliary equivalence after transport between equal quiver structures.
An auxiliary modification of a quiver-indexed object at a chosen vertex.
Under the auxiliary vertex condition, the two displayed dependent-pair types are equivalent.
The auxiliary map from the second displayed dependent-pair type to the first.
The auxiliary map preserves the first projection.
Applying the auxiliary map to the pair formed from an element's first projection and its auxiliary quiver morphism recovers the element.
The first projection of every element of the auxiliary dependent-pair type differs from the distinguished vertex.
The quiver morphism from the first projection of an auxiliary dependent pair to the distinguished vertex.
A family of linear equivalences induces a linear equivalence between the corresponding direct sums.
The direct-sum linear equivalence sends a vector inserted in one summand to the insertion of its image in the corresponding summand.
A componentwise direct-sum equivalence carries the range of the first displayed sum of composites onto the range of the second.
An injective map followed by a surjective map has range equal to kernel when the range lies in the kernel and the endpoint finranks add to the middle finrank.
The first auxiliary condition at a vertex implies the second auxiliary condition.
The second auxiliary condition at a vertex implies the first auxiliary condition.
The auxiliary morphism of the auxiliary image of a dependent pair is its second projection.
An auxiliary equivalence remains inhabited after applying the displayed vertex-dependent transformation to both related objects.
An auxiliary equivalence induces a linear equivalence between the two displayed vertex-indexed modules after the indicated transformation.
The auxiliary operation on a morphism from the distinguished vertex to a distinct vertex agrees with the indicated cast.
Under the auxiliary vertex condition, applying the incoming auxiliary operation after the outgoing one recovers the original morphism.
The auxiliary morphism of a pair built from a distinct vertex and its transformed incoming morphism is the original morphism.
The auxiliary operation on a morphism from a distinct vertex to the distinguished vertex agrees with the indicated cast.
The auxiliary operation on a morphism whose endpoints both differ from the distinguished vertex agrees with the indicated cast.
Applying the auxiliary operation twice to a morphism between vertices away from the distinguished vertex recovers that morphism.
The auxiliary quiver structure associated with a chosen vertex is equal to the original quiver structure.

If the displayed canonical map at the distinguished vertex is surjective, then a linear map out of the indexed direct sum is surjective whenever every vector transported along the displayed quiver morphisms has a preimage.
For the displayed transformed object, the finite sum of the indicated composites of quiver-induced linear maps is zero.
